stage_a.note: The founders maintain a bright, upbeat delivery with frequent smiles and positive engagement throughout.
They use animated gestures and energetic vocal delivery to convey excitement about their solution.
Their presentation style is friendly and approachable, connecting well as they introduce themselves as moms.

venture.description: Premium, perfectly portioned seafood delivered directly to consumers' doors, with simple thawing and cooking instructions.
venture.note: The ask is stated early in the pitch.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founders introduce themselves, state their ask, explain the problem of low seafood consumption, and present their delivery solution.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Lori asks the founders if the panel can eat the food placed in front of them.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Emily enthusiastically confirms that the sharks should eat the food.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Emily describes the various seafood dishes the sharks are tasting, including shrimp, crab cake, and salmon.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Lori comments positively on the taste of the sauce.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Robert expresses that the food is awesome.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Kevin jokes that they are doing a very good job of sucking up by serving a specific wine.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Robert asks the founders about their background and how they started the business.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Emily explains her extensive career in the seafood business, including starting a live lobster wholesale distribution facility.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Lori asks how Emily's background in wholesale seafood morphed into their current consumer business.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Emily details how she met Melissa and transitioned into working for a large wine and spirits wholesaler.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Lori asks Emily whether it is harder to sell spirits or fish.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Emily responds that both require storytelling and connecting with the customer.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Mark asks if they are exclusively a subscription service or if products can be bought individually.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Emily clarifies that customers can buy anything on the website, with subscriptions set up for convenience.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Robert asks for a breakdown of their costs and pricing.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Emily provides the retail price of their most popular 16-portion box, addressing price but not yet cost.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Robert asks for their total sales figure.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Melissa states that they did $821,000 in sales last year.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Mark asks if they made any money from those sales.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Melissa confirms they made a profit of $20,000.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Kevin asks what their customer acquisition cost is, suspecting it is the reason for low profits.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Melissa states their customer acquisition cost is between $30 and $40.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Rohan asks what their projected sales look like for the current year.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Melissa shares their year-to-date sales and forecasts they will break a million, hoping to land around 1.2 million.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Rohan asks for a breakdown of their manufacturing and delivery costs to understand their total landed cost.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Melissa explains their average order value and their current high delivered cost, indicating they want to discuss it.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Rohan asks what the reason is behind their high delivered costs.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Melissa explains they subsidize shipping to the coasts, which became an issue as their customer mix shifted significantly.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Lori acknowledges that their margin issue is entirely due to shipping costs.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Melissa confirms it's shipping, noting that shipping consumes 11% of their revenue.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Kevin asks what their plan is to resolve the shipping issue.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Melissa outlines a plan to use a 3PL to strategically reach every zone quickly, fitting their model.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Mark explains that the highly variable costs of seafood and shipping make the business too tough, and exits.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Rohan asks about their repeat order rate among existing customers.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Emily states that 55% of customers have returned and 70% of revenue comes from subscriptions.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Robert states he lacks expertise in shipping and logistics to help them, and exits.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Kevin offers the requested money for a third of the business, leveraging his Chef Wonderful brand.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Emily responds confidently to Kevin's star comment, noting they are Division One athletes.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Rohan exits, stating they need a partner who understands the logistics of moving fish.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Lori exits, advising them not to give away equity and to find money elsewhere for distribution centers.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Kevin jokes about being the last fish left for them to swim to.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Kevin pressures them to decide, stating he has no flexibility and wants a third.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Emily asks Kevin to confirm that he has absolutely no flexibility on his offer.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Kevin firmly states he has no flexibility.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Robert encourages Melissa to make a counter offer anyway.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Emily counters Kevin's offer, asking if he would do the deal for 25%.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Kevin rejects Emily's counter offer.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Kevin revises his offer, agreeing to do the deal for 30% equity.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Melissa verifies that Kevin is willing to do the deal for 30%.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Emily asks if Kevin will fund purchase orders to help them get into distribution.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Kevin says he won't commit until he sees their financials, noting CAC is the real issue.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Melissa asks Kevin about the demographic breakdown of his Chef Wonderful audience.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Kevin answers that his chef business audience is majority women.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Robert jokes that the founders are so good they have Kevin begging them.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Kevin suggests they look up Chef Wonderful online to verify his reach.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Robert asks Melissa if she is going to give up 30% of the business.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Lori interjects to ask if they have considered using social media chefs for marketing.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Kevin teases Lori, telling her to make an offer if she wants to interject.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Mark advises the founders that Kevin's offer provides valuable resources they are currently lacking.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Emily reiterates their counter of 25%, emphasizing their value and hard work.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Kevin urges them to accept his 30% offer for a new lease on life in the business.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Emily pushes back, stating that they do not do failure.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Kevin reiterates that his brand prevents failure and firmly holds his offer at 30%.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Lori tells the founders she does not want them doing the deal for 30%.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Kevin dismissively tells Lori he doesn't care what she wants.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Lori re-enters the negotiation, offering exactly the founders' ask to save them from Kevin's deal.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Emily immediately accepts Lori's offer.

decisions.note: Variable costs of seafood and shipping make the business too tough.
Does not know enough about shipping and logistics to help them.
Successful model, wants to make them stars, requires a third of the business.
They need a partner who understands moving fish, which is not him.
They don't need to give away equity, can get money elsewhere.
Counters Kevin's offer asking for 25% equity.
Reiterates counter of 25% emphasizing their efficiency and value.
Re-enters to offer exactly what the founders are asking for to save them from Kevin.
